# Copilot Instructions for node-version-statusbar

1. **Purpose**: VS Code extension shows the active Node.js version in the status bar and lets users refresh, copy, install, and switch versions via `NodeVersionProvider` (see `src/extension.ts`).
2. **Primary file**: `src/extension.ts` holds activation, command registrations (`nodeVersion.refresh|copyVersion|switchVersion|installVersion`), and the `NodeVersionProvider` class. No other source files exist.
3. **Build/Test workflow**: Use npm scripts from `package.json` – `npm run compile` (tsc build), `npm run watch`, `npm run lint`, `npm run test`. During development launch the Extension Development Host via VS Code `F5` (per `README.md`).
4. **Status bar lifecycle**: `NodeVersionProvider` creates a left-aligned status bar item, shows/hides it based on `nodeVersion.showInStatusBar`, and refreshes text according to the `nodeVersion.statusBarText` template (defaults to `$(symbol-method) Node {version}`).
5. **Refresh flow**: `refresh()` → `getNodeVersion()` (`node --version`, fallback to `npx node --version` scoped to first workspace folder) → `updateStatusBar()` handles success, warning (no Node), or error (uses theme colors & tooltip messaging). Avoid changing this sequence unless adding new fallbacks.
6. **Version managers**: Only `nvm` (Windows/macOS/Linux) and `n` (macOS/Linux) are supported today. `initializeVersionManagers()` wires each with `{name, command, listCommand, listRemote, useCommand}` and marks availability via `manager --version` (special-case Windows nvm via `cmd /c`). `n` never registers on Windows and any new manager must follow the same structure, including a `listRemote` command for installs.
7. **Version discovery**: `getAvailableVersions()` iterates over `availableManagers`, calling `getVersionsForManager()` and deduping versions by string (active entries sorted first). Parsing logic per manager lives in `parseVersionLine`; update there when adjusting CLI output formats.
8. **Switch workflow**: `showVersionPicker()` builds QuickPick entries annotated with manager names, then `switchToVersion()` opens a dedicated terminal (CMD `/K` on Windows) to run the selected manager’s `use` command, displays progress, tries `verifyVersionSwitch()`, and prompts for a VS Code reload. Maintain this workflow for new managers (command, progress, verification, cleanup).
9. **Install workflow**: `installNewVersion()` selects a manager, runs a remote listing command (`listRemote`), and shows the results in a QuickPick (with a manual-entry fallback) before kicking off manager-specific install commands inside a terminal plus progress UI and final refresh. Follow the same branching style (`switch (manager.name)`) for additional managers and ensure remote listing degrades gracefully.
10. **Windows specifics**: Windows is detected via `os.platform() === "win32"`. For nvm on Windows, `getNvmPath()` searches `NVM_HOME`, `%APPDATA%\nvm`, or `where nvm.exe`. Switching/installation uses `cmd.exe` with `call "<nvmPath>" ... & echo %ERRORLEVEL%`. Do **not** assume POSIX shell availability when `isWindows` is true.
11. **Configuration keys**: Settings live under `nodeVersion.*` (`showInStatusBar`, `statusBarText`, `refreshInterval`, `preferredManager`, `showSwitchButton`) per `README.md`. Respect these when adding behaviors (e.g., new template tokens must degrade gracefully).
12. **Error handling & UX**: Console log errors (already using `console.error`/`console.warn`) and surface user-facing messages via `vscode.window.showInformationMessage/ErrorMessage/WarningMessage`. Status bar warnings should continue to leverage theme colors for clarity.
13. **Dependencies/APIs**: Uses Node built-ins (`child_process.exec` via `promisify`, `fs`, `path`, `os`). VS Code APIs include `window.createStatusBarItem`, `commands.registerCommand`, QuickPick, Progress notifications, and Terminals. Keep new async flows `await`ed to avoid dangling promises.
14. **Formatting & Standards**: TypeScript, strict-ish style (no semicolons). Keep code comments minimal but helpful; prefer descriptive method/variable names. Follow existing pattern of template literals and string interpolation.
15. **Testing expectations**: No automated tests exist; manual verification via Extension Development Host is standard. When altering manager logic, instruct users to test on macOS/Linux + Windows (if relevant) especially around terminals, reload prompts, and `getNodeVersion` fallbacks.
